title: Azure tenant-root access elevation succeeded
description: Detects successful use of the Azure administrative elevateAccess operation at tenant root.

hypothesis.summary: A privileged actor may use tenant-root access elevation to gain Azure resource-management access across subscriptions; the event also occurs during legitimate recovery.
hypothesis.rationale: The operation records an elevation workflow, not compromise. Global administrators may legitimately elevate for recovery and access management.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Detects successful use of the Azure administrative elevateAccess operation at tenant root.

triage.summary: The operation records an elevation workflow, not compromise. Global administrators may legitimately elevate for recovery and access management.
steps: Review the operation, resource, caller, source address and correlation ID; establish the approved change or recovery owner.
Inspect effective post-change configuration and independent controls, then correlate related role, resource and logging changes.
Validate the business justification and restore the affected control or contain unauthorized access through the consumer's approved process.
false_positives: Approved Global Administrator recovery, tenant access review or emergency access management.

validation.expected_outcome: Match the bounded event, key/action/path or successful operation combination; reject one-field mutations, lookalikes and absent required fields. Synthetic tests do not establish live telemetry or production performance.

limitations: The operation records an elevation workflow, not compromise. Global administrators may legitimately elevate for recovery and access management.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
